column1: # Original WritingDeck plots; MIT to the extent rights subsist; AI-assisted original drafting.
# stable_id|category|genres|premise

wd-p-0852|status|realist,satire|A restaurant accidentally prints a menu describing the staff's private names for its dishes. Customers love the apparent honesty, and the owner asks the person most offended by the names to develop the new brand.

wd-p-0853|coordination|realist,satire|A town elects a dog as honorary mayor to avoid political arguments. Its owner receives conflicting invitations, and choosing which ceremony the dog attends becomes the most divisive decision of the year.

wd-p-0854|consent|realist,satire|A couple lets wedding guests suggest activities anonymously. Every suggestion is designed to avoid another guest, and the resulting schedule would prevent anyone from attending the ceremony together.

wd-p-0855|craft|realist,satire|An amateur choir becomes famous for an accidental silence during a performance. Its next audience demands the same effect, but nobody agrees whether repeating a mistake faithfully means rehearsing it.

wd-p-0856|value|realist,satire|A secondhand shop labels an ordinary chair as mysterious to attract attention. Buyers invent elaborate histories, and the employee who knows its mundane origin is invited to authenticate the most profitable story.

wd-p-0857|measurement|realist,satire|A town holds a competition for the shortest speech. The winner submits no words, but accepting the prize requires a public explanation long enough to disqualify the entry.

wd-p-0858|identity|realist,satire|Two neighboring businesses exchange signs during renovations and each becomes more successful. Restoring the names would correct the street while forcing both owners to explain why customers liked the wrong promise better.

wd-p-0859|recognition|realist,satire|A local artist paints a flattering group portrait from separate photographs. At the unveiling, every person claims the least flattering figure is someone else, and the missing sitter recognizes herself in the only empty chair.

wd-p-0860|reciprocity|realist,satire|A neighborhood starts leaving unwanted surplus produce on one another's doorsteps. The same enormous squash circulates for weeks until a child records its journey and asks who will finally accept the gift.

wd-p-0861|access|realist,satire|A club advertises that everyone is welcome but keeps its location secret to preserve atmosphere. The secretary charged with recruiting members must make the venue findable without ruining the exclusivity members call friendliness.

wd-p-0862|coordination|realist,satire|A community play assigns small speaking roles to avoid favoritism. Everyone adds a sentence to clarify their character, and the prompter becomes the only person who still knows which story is being performed.

wd-p-0863|status|realist,satire|A resident invents a ceremonial title to make a volunteer job easier. The title attracts ambitious applicants, and the inventor must decide whether to reveal that its grand responsibilities consist mainly of carrying folding chairs.

wd-p-0864|craft|realist,satire|A pottery class agrees to exhibit only imperfect work to reduce pressure. Students begin carefully producing attractive flaws, leaving the genuine beginner embarrassed by a pot that is simply uneven.

wd-p-0865|choice|realist,satire|A town asks residents to name a new bridge, then discovers the winning suggestion refers to the bridge it replaced. The organizer can accept the vote only by making every future set of directions less clear.

wd-p-0866|permission|realist,satire|A café lets customers choose the music one song at a time. A patient regular uses perfectly cheerful songs to drive away another customer, and the owner must explain why compliance with the rule can still be inhospitable.

wd-p-0867|attention|realist,satire|A lecturer's lost notes are replaced by an audience member's shopping list. The audience interprets the improvised talk as an ingenious metaphor, and the lecturer is asked to publish the argument she never intended.

wd-p-0868|resources|realist,satire|A library's fundraiser sells sponsorship of individual shelves. Sponsors request that their shelves contain only flattering books, leaving the librarian with a growing collection of unplaceable titles about ordinary human mistakes.

wd-p-0869|learning|realist,satire|A beginner's cooking class becomes popular because the instructor demonstrates how to recover failures. A flawless session disappoints everyone, and the instructor is tempted to ruin a meal to satisfy the promise of reassurance.

wd-p-0870|trust|realist,satire|A guest invents expertise in a harmless hobby to keep a conversation moving. The host organizes a public demonstration as a surprise thank-you, and the guest's only possible teacher is the person whose work they casually criticized.

wd-p-0871|ownership|realist,satire|A communal fridge labels food by the name of the person who should eat it. Two residents use the system to care for each other while each assumes the other's gifts are reminders of a dietary rule.

wd-p-0872|performance|realist,satire|A town reenacts its founding argument without agreeing which side won. The performers discover that the original dispute concerned the cost of holding an annual reenactment, making the production itself the strongest evidence for one side.

wd-p-0873|coordination|realist,satire|A dinner host assigns seats to prevent familiar arguments. The arrangement introduces people who discover a new disagreement shared across every old alliance, and the host must decide whether the lively evening counts as success.

wd-p-0874|status|realist,satire|A repair volunteer is mistaken for a visiting expert and treated with unusual respect. Correcting the title would restore honesty but also end the attention finally being paid to advice she has offered for years.

wd-p-0875|craft|realist,satire|A flower show introduces a category for plants that survived neglect. Careful gardeners begin deliberately neglecting entries, while the person whose accidental survivor inspired the category is disqualified for watering it on the final day.

wd-p-0876|choice|realist,satire|A club agrees that its next outing will be chosen at random. The person drawing the destination recognizes her own handwriting on every slip and must explain why she copied everyone else's suggestions without changing them.

wd-p-0877|permission|realist,satire|A family appoints a relative to enforce a rule against discussing work at dinner. The enforcer's only recent news is the new responsibility, which nobody can praise without inviting the discussion they were chosen to stop.

wd-p-0878|attention|realist,satire|A museum labels one empty case as an invitation to imagine. Visitors begin leaving objects, and the curator must choose between protecting the emptiness and acknowledging the unplanned collection that made people participate.

wd-p-0879|resources|realist,satire|A town buys a giant ceremonial ribbon to save money on many small openings. The ribbon is scheduled at two ceremonies simultaneously, and neither organizer will accept being described as the less important event.

wd-p-0880|learning|realist,satire|A public-speaking group praises every speech to build confidence. A new member sincerely asks which part needs work, exposing that nobody has practiced offering the useful criticism the group was founded to make less frightening.

wd-p-0881|trust|realist,satire|A host promises a visiting writer complete privacy, then asks neighbors not to reveal the visit. The coordinated secrecy attracts more attention than any announcement, and the host becomes the person everyone consults for confirmation.

wd-p-0882|ownership|realist,satire|A neighborhood borrows a ladder so often that nobody remembers its owner. A resident buys a replacement to end the uncertainty, and three people claim the new ladder as compensation for having once supplied the old one.

wd-p-0883|performance|realist,satire|A silent auction is conducted in a room where the organizer cannot stop announcing how silent everyone should be. The highest bidder offers to buy the microphone if the bid can count as a donation.

wd-p-0884|coordination|realist,satire|A family organizes a surprise reunion through separate message groups. Every group excludes a different organizer, producing five sincere plans that all require the same relative to arrive somewhere else first.

wd-p-0885|status|realist,satire|An office awards the title of most approachable employee. The winner becomes too busy receiving unrelated requests to perform the work that made her approachable, while declining a request now looks like refusing the honor.

wd-p-0886|craft|realist,satire|A carpenter makes a deliberately crooked display shelf for an art project. Customers want the mistake repeated precisely, turning the advertisement for freedom from perfection into the most exacting order in the workshop.

wd-p-0887|choice|realist,satire|A café allows regulars to name a new drink by consensus. They agree on a name nobody likes because each thinks someone else proposed it, and the server discovers the misunderstanding after the menu is printed.

wd-p-0888|permission|realist,satire|A town installs a noticeboard for spontaneous announcements. A volunteer creates an approval form to keep it tidy, and the first rejected notice announces a gathering to discuss whether the board still serves its purpose.

wd-p-0889|attention|realist,satire|A photographer advertises portraits showing people as they really are. Every customer requests an alteration that feels more truthful than the camera, and the photographer must explain why literal accuracy was mistaken for honest recognition.

wd-p-0890|resources|realist,satire|A club offers free tea to encourage attendance. Members arrive early enough to consume the budget before the meeting, forcing the treasurer to choose between charging for the welcome and admitting the meeting itself is not the attraction.

wd-p-0891|learning|realist,satire|A workshop teaches efficient packing using an empty demonstration suitcase. The instructor's own case bursts open afterward, revealing that the perfect system excluded every object she personally could not leave behind.

wd-p-0892|trust|realist,satire|A neighborhood's anonymous compliment campaign begins praising people for things they have never done. The organizer discovers that the notes describe aspirations overheard at a planning meeting rather than completed acts.

wd-p-0893|ownership|realist,satire|A small theater rents a prop throne to several community groups. Its booking calendar reveals that rival leaders have each been photographed claiming the same chair as a unique symbol of their authority.

wd-p-0894|performance|realist,satire|A band is hired to play unobtrusive background music. When the audience applauds an accidental pause, the musicians disagree about whether to continue playing or repeat the silence that finally earned recognition.

wd-p-0895|coordination|realist,satire|A village meal assigns dishes alphabetically by surname. A family name change suddenly leaves the meal without a main course, and the organizer must decide whether the cheerful rule matters more than the shared dinner.

wd-p-0896|status|realist,satire|A tour guide invents a modest anecdote about an unremarkable doorway. The story becomes the town's favorite attraction, and an actual resident of the doorway asks the guide to invent something that gives her a less inconvenient role.

wd-p-0897|craft|realist,satire|A hobbyist's unfinished model wins a prize for minimalism. Completing it would destroy the work the judges admired, while leaving it unfinished would make the prize a reward for an interruption rather than the intended design.

wd-p-0898|choice|realist,satire|A committee promises to choose the plainest possible uniform. The resulting argument over what counts as plain becomes more elaborate than any design submitted, and the tailor's deadline approaches without a wearable decision.

wd-p-0899|permission|realist,satire|A workplace encourages staff to decorate desks with personal interests. An employee displays an interest in labor history, and the manager asks for something less political without noticing the military memorabilia on neighboring desks.

wd-p-0900|attention|realist,satire|A town begins rating the friendliness of its shops. Employees become so busy greeting visitors that transactions slow, and the least highly rated shop is the one quietly helping customers finish their errands.

wd-p-0901|resources|realist,satire|A community festival borrows equipment under agreements to return it cleaner than received. Volunteers polish away the chalk labels needed to identify the owners, making exemplary care the cause of an ownership dispute.

wd-p-0902|learning|realist,satire|A language learner practices polite refusals so convincingly that the teacher stops offering invitations. Restoring the friendship requires a sentence the formal lesson never covered: a refusal of the assumption that every refusal is permanent.

wd-p-0903|trust|realist,satire|An amateur magician promises a trick with no deception. The audience supplies elaborate explanations for an ordinary action, and the magician must choose whether correcting them will disappoint the expectation the promise created.

wd-p-0904|ownership|realist,satire|A town declares one bench everyone's property. Residents begin making improvements without consultation until the bench can no longer be sat on, and removing any addition is treated as disrespecting its donor.

wd-p-0905|performance|realist,satire|A choir is hired to imitate an old recording. The recording contains a cough by a now-celebrated singer, and the conductor must decide whether historical faithfulness requires assigning someone the embarrassing sound.

wd-p-0906|coordination|realist,satire|A club introduces secret ballots for every minor decision. The secretary receives identical handwriting on every ballot because members asked the same helpful person to fill them in, defeating anonymity without any dishonest vote.

wd-p-0907|status|realist,satire|A resident gains a reputation for modesty after refusing an award. The committee creates a larger award for the refusal, and accepting or declining now seems to strengthen the public story he wanted to avoid.

wd-p-0908|craft|realist,satire|A chef gives away a recipe described as impossible to get wrong. A customer finds a completely reasonable substitution that fails, and the chef is asked to apologize without turning a welcoming promise into a list of exclusions.

wd-p-0909|choice|realist,satire|A town chooses its festival date by avoiding every religious and civic occasion. The only remaining day coincides with the anniversary of the meeting that created the festival, which members have separately promised to keep free.

wd-p-0910|permission|realist,satire|A landlord permits harmless pets but insists each animal be individually approved. A tenant submits a tank of tiny organisms used for a school project, and the application cannot describe their number before reproduction changes it.

wd-p-0911|attention|realist,satire|An art class practices observing overlooked objects. The town then removes every shabby object students sketch, and the teacher realizes the well-received project is being used as an unofficial cleanup survey.

wd-p-0912|resources|realist,satire|A meeting's refreshments are funded according to attendance. Members invite extra friends to improve the budget, then discover that the new guests have acquired the right to vote on how the refreshments are chosen.

wd-p-0913|learning|realist,satire|A confidence coach asks participants to introduce themselves without mentioning work. The coach cannot complete the exercise and must decide whether the admission will undermine the lesson or finally demonstrate it honestly.

wd-p-0914|trust|realist,satire|A resident publishes a list of reliable local businesses based on personal favors. One listed shop refuses a reasonable request, exposing that reliability was measured by a friendship nobody else can use.

wd-p-0915|ownership|realist,satire|A community group receives a donated trophy with space for only one winner. It chooses to reward cooperation, then spends the season arguing over whose name should represent the cooperative success.

wd-p-0916|performance|realist,satire|A town hires a professional listener for a day of public complaints. Residents become so pleased to be heard that they keep returning with improved versions, and the listener must ask whether resolution would end the service they actually value.

wd-p-0917|coordination|realist,satire|A restaurant divides its waiting list into people in a hurry and people willing to wait. Everyone claims patience to appear considerate, leaving the host unable to identify the diners whose actual deadlines have become urgent.

wd-p-0918|status|realist,satire|A local expert is invited to judge a competition in a field she knows little about because organizers confuse her name with another person's. Her careful questions improve the judging, making correction feel harder with every compliment.

wd-p-0919|craft|realist,satire|A printer offers a discount for accepting a random ink color. A customer receives exactly the color she wanted and insists the promised randomness has been violated, turning a lucky outcome into a contractual dispute.

wd-p-0920|choice|realist,satire|A bookshop's blind-date books are wrapped with descriptions instead of titles. The owner recognizes a returning customer who keeps choosing the same disliked book under increasingly accurate descriptions.

wd-p-0921|permission|realist,satire|A family agrees that anyone may propose a new tradition. The first proposal is to stop calling activities traditions before anyone has enjoyed them twice, and the debate becomes the gathering's most repeated activity.

wd-p-0922|attention|realist,satire|A museum introduces a quiet hour so visitors can reflect. Staff spend the hour making repeated announcements about the silence, and the attendant who turns off the speaker is reprimanded for failing to provide information.

wd-p-0923|resources|realist,satire|A charity dinner offers larger portions to higher-paying donors. The kitchen's volunteer mistakes generous giving for greater hunger, and correcting the service would make the fundraiser's priorities visible on every plate.

wd-p-0924|learning|realist,satire|An etiquette instructor is asked to teach a welcoming ritual unfamiliar to her. Rather than admit uncertainty, she invents a simpler version, then meets the person whose family practice the client hoped to honor.

wd-p-0925|trust|realist,satire|A town places a trust-based payment box beside public equipment. The box fills with notes explaining why people owe nothing, and the caretaker must distinguish honest exceptions from a system that no longer funds repairs.

wd-p-0926|ownership|realist,satire|A borrowed umbrella passes through so many helpful hands that its owner receives an invitation to a ceremony celebrating the unknown person who supplied it. Claiming it would end the town's favorite mystery and reclaim the only umbrella still missing from home.
